rationale:
ROUND 2. Round 1 came back REVISE and BOTH objections were correct; this answers them.

OBJECTION 1 (editquality, medium): allow_reinstall was 'safe but inert -- no edit sets it true or wires any handler to it'. On checking it was worse than inert. The flag was read from StepConfig.Config ONLY, and site-design-planner's install step config holds nothing but path references, so the only way to switch it on was to edit the AGENT DEFINITION -- which turns re-install on for EVERY composition install fleet-wide, the exact unsafe-default-ON state the flag exists to prevent. There was no way to re-compose ONE site. FIXED: the flag is now also read per-request from the dispatching work item's spec (collected_data.input_data.spec, with the .body.spec wrapper handled), so a single needs_composition item can carry allow_reinstall=true and nobody else's behaviour changes. Both sources default false and both go through GetBoolFieldLoud, so a malformed declaration in EITHER falls back to the safe branch. New test D fails if the per-request branch is removed (mutation run, 2026-08-11); new test E proves the per-request channel is exactly as strict as the step-config one.

OBJECTION 2 (bug_historian, gating): I cited work item 47ce091c as a needs_composition/needs_design blockage created 2026-08-06. The seat's own read-only query showed it is item_type needs_design_review, item_key shared_style_ai-agent-orchestration.com, created 2026-04-24 -- I had read updated_at as the creation date. The 'triaged' edit does NOT unblock it and never could. WITHDRAWN. The sites that edit actually unblocks are noted.co.uk, loanandmortgagecalculator.co.uk and loancalculator.co.uk -- three sites, six rows, none of them ai-agent-orchestration.com. The edit itself still stands on its own merits: emit_design_items_action.go:126,171 emits needs_composition/needs_design as 'triaged' and check_integrity.go emitted the SAME two item_keys as 'detected', while claim_work_item_action.go:102 claims only triaged/approved -- two producers of one item_key disagreeing. Only my evidence was wrong, and it is logged in WRONG_CALLS.md.

ALSO CORRECTED: I sized the mismatch pattern at 448 detected build-pipeline rows. The seat's query shows it spans other pipelines too (undeployed_asset 86 design, phantom_internal_link 18 content, unbuilt_internal_link 17 content, image_url_404 16 design). The conclusion is unchanged and stronger: do NOT fix this by enabling a fleet-wide triage sweep.

SCOPE NOTE (owner ruling RFC_022, 2026-08-11): this is an opt-in field whose unsafe side is the default and which NO live consumer names -- enumerated, not asserted: zero rows in agent_definitions match 'allow_reinstall'. Per that ruling this shape is not architecture-scope.

Round 1's code is already live (chassis stamp bb534864, my commit 5c7b115c5 is an ancestor, verified by binary probe with present/absent controls on both replicas). So this round is a revision of shipped code, not a proposal.

plan.summary: ROUND 2. Round 1 shipped allow_reinstall but it was readable only from step config, making it settable only by an agent-definition edit that would turn re-install on fleet-wide -- so it could not repair the one site it was built for. This adds the per-request source (the work item's spec), keeps both defaults false and both reads loud-fallback, and withdraws the round-1 evidence claim about work item 47ce091c, which was a different item_type than I said and is not unblocked by the 'triaged' edit.

edits.rationale: Add allow_reinstall as an opt-in step-config literal, default FALSE, per the owner ruling of 2026-08-02 (RFC_010): new authority on a shared seam ships as an opt-in field with the unsafe default OFF, not as a documented contract. Read via GetBoolFieldLoud so a malformed declaration (string "true") warns and falls back to the SAFE branch rather than enabling the permissive one. Deliberately NOT added to the ActionInputSpec: ExtractActionInputs resolves config strings as PATH REFERENCES into collected_data, which is right for data inputs and wrong for an author's literal switch.

Keep the concurrent-install race guard working in BOTH modes. The link UPDATE was guarded by 'AND style_collection_id IS NULL', which is exactly the condition the reinstall path violates. Dropping the guard would silently clobber a concurrent install; the reinstall path needs the race check MORE than the first-install path, not less. IS NOT DISTINCT FROM matches NULL to NULL on a first install and the observed id to itself on a reinstall.
edits.sketch:
-  AND style_collection_id IS NULL
+  AND style_collection_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $3::uuid

edits.rationale: Three tests, PROVEN load-bearing by mutation rather than asserted to be. A: an existing collection is refused when nothing asked for a reinstall (this is the test that keeps the unsafe direction off, and it is the important one). B: the flag gets execution past the guard. C: a non-bool declaration must NOT enable the permissive branch. Mutations were RUN before commit: 'if !allowReinstall' -> 'if false' fails A and C; hardcoding allowReinstall=false fails B. Tests stop at the guard rather than mocking the whole install, and the file says so -- claiming more than the mock can support is how a test becomes decoration.

MissingStyleCollectionCheck emits the composition pair as 'triaged' instead of 'detected', matching emit_design_items_action.go:126,171 -- which emits the SAME two item_keys, and which this check's own comment already claims parity with. Scoped to these two types on purpose: the defect is the disagreement between two producers of one item_key, so the repair belongs at the producer, NOT at a fleet-wide triage sweep that would promote all 448 detected build rows in one motion.

edits.rationale: THE ROUND-1 FIX. Read allow_reinstall per-request from the dispatching work item's spec as well as from step config, so ONE site can be re-composed without turning re-install on fleet-wide. Step config is checked first and the spec only consulted when it did not opt in; both default false and both go through GetBoolFieldLoud, so a malformed value in either falls back to the SAFE branch. A new helper resolves input_data.spec and the input_data.body.spec wrapper, returning nil rather than an empty map so 'no spec' and 'a spec that says nothing' stay distinguishable in a reader's eyes.

Two tests for the per-request channel, both proven load-bearing by mutation run 2026-08-11: making the spec lookup return nil fails D ALONE, leaving A/B/C/E passing. D asserts a work-item spec can opt in; E asserts a malformed value there falls back to the safe branch, because a work item spec is assembled by whatever queued it and is the easier place to get this wrong.

plan.risks: (1) The flag now has TWO sources. Check the precedence is harmless: step config is read first and the spec is consulted only if it did not opt in, so the two cannot disagree into a surprising result -- but confirm you agree that EITHER saying true is sufficient. (2) requestSpecFromCollected guesses at two shapes (input_data.spec, input_data.body.spec). If the dispatch loop produces a third, the flag silently does not arrive and the caller gets the refusal -- which is the SAFE direction, but it will look like the flag is broken. I have NOT observed a live needs_composition dispatch's collected_data shape; that is unmeasured. (3) Still no live consumer sets the flag -- deliberate. The repair for ai-agent-orchestration.com is a work item carrying spec.allow_reinstall=true, queued AFTER this rolls. (4) Round 1's code is already live, so a REJECTED here means reverting shipped behaviour, not declining a proposal. (5) The orphaned old css_theme / style_collection rows after a re-compose are still not reaped; unchanged from round 1 and still unmeasured.
